title: Tirion and Taelan: Of Love and Family
summary: Tirion asks a stranger to help his son remember his family and honor. A childhood gift, a lost emblem and Renfray’s portrait reach Taelan in Hearthglen; his choice to leave ends in death and gives Tirion a renewed purpose.
opening: At the edge of the Plaguelands, an exile entrusts his son’s past to a stranger. Keepsakes carry a father’s hope into Hearthglen, where a choice to return leads toward the loss Tirion must bear.

chapters.title: An Exile’s Request
chapters.body:
In the cold Eastern Plaguelands, an old hermit accepted help before offering his name. Among the countryside’s dangers, a stranger earned his trust. At the riverbank, another wound waited beyond the work of survival: a family’s long absence. The land had lost much to plague and war; the hermit carried a loss whose living answer remained close enough to hope for.

The hermit was Tirion Fordring, convicted of treason and banished from the Alliance. He had remained near his son. Taelan had become lord of Mardenholde and a Highlord of the Scarlet Crusade, an order Tirion believed fallen from the Silver Hand’s purpose. The exiled father asked for help. He hoped the honor they had once shared still endured beneath his son’s service.

In the Undercroft lay a miniature warhammer Tirion had once given Taelan. It was bound to a false grave and the childhood belief that his father was dead. Small enough for a young hand, the keepsake carried years of separation beneath a lie. Its recovery could not restore those years. It offered one remembered gift to place before the son who had grown beyond it.

After Uther’s death, Taelan had stood at Northdale and laid down the Silver Hand’s standard. Its emblem rested beneath the lake. Tirion asked that it be recovered. From dark water, the small sign of an abandoned allegiance returned to the living. Beside the childhood hammer, it could recall a part of Taelan’s own honor that the Scarlet Crusade had not created.

chapters.title: What the Portrait Keeps
chapters.body:
Tirion remembered happier family days and the portrait painted by his friend Renfray. At Caer Darrow, the artist’s ghost remained among the island’s ruins. Her work had preserved a likeness of people since divided by death and exile. The seeker came for that surviving canvas, hoping a memory once set in paint could still reach the son its subjects had lost.

Renfray’s direction led into Stratholme. In the Archivist’s room, the Fordring family portrait lay hidden behind a picture of twin moons. Amid the ruined city, a small work of family memory had survived. The search that began with a child’s gift and an abandoned emblem now recovered the faces of a life Taelan had once known.

The painting returned with Karandra and young Taelan beside Tirion. It restored their likeness without returning their lost years. For the exiled father, memory could at last be placed within his son’s reach. If Taelan would receive it, the portrait might recall a belonging older than the Scarlet banners under which he now served.

At Uther’s Tomb, Myranda received Tirion’s appeal and the gathered keepsakes. His former ally could help the seeker enter Hearthglen. Against pale memorial stone and plague-damaged grass, the father’s hope passed into another’s care. Beyond that last preparation, the old family tokens would be carried directly to Taelan, beneath the colors of the order Tirion feared had claimed him.

chapters.title: Dreams and Departure
chapters.body:
A disguise opened the way into Hearthglen. Under borrowed Scarlet colors, the seeker brought Tirion’s package to Taelan. The father remained in exile while the memories he had gathered crossed the guarded threshold. Within the stronghold, the portrait, hammer and emblem reached the Highlord. What they might awaken belonged to the son who received them.

Taelan recognized how long he had served as the Grand Crusader’s instrument. His father’s memory had endured beneath that service, and he chose to leave Hearthglen. The keepsakes offered a past from which he could make that choice. Red-and-white standards still surrounded him, but their claim upon his future had broken. The way toward Tirion now lay beyond the hall.

Taelan left the keep, and Scarlet Crusade forces opposed his departure. He had chosen to break with the order that shaped his adult life. Through Hearthglen, the struggle carried him toward the open road. Beyond the settlement stood a tower. The journey toward his father had become an ordeal, with the allegiance he had abandoned barring his way.

At the roadside tower, Grand Inquisitor Isillien killed Taelan. The son who had chosen to leave the Scarlet Crusade could no longer return to the father he hoped to meet. A small human post stood amid the wounded land, marking the end of that road. The long labor to restore memory had reached a cost no recovered keepsake could answer.

Tirion reached the tower too late. He defeated Isillien and grieved beside Taelan. The appeal begun at Thondroril had brought the father back into his son’s life only at its ending. Truth had been recovered, but the living voice that might have answered was gone. Beside the body, the old hope of reunion gave way to a grief that would demand another purpose.

At Taelan’s body, Tirion vowed to gather a new Order of the Silver Hand and return it to the defense of the world. The honor his son had once laid down could still guide the living. The vow did not undo the loss beside the tower. It carried the father’s grief beyond exile, toward a duty whose fulfillment still lay ahead.
